_note: These are fictional recurring editorial characters who are part of Seasonal's voice. They are not real people and carry no real credentials, biographies, locations, employers, or factual claims about their lives. Each character represents a consistent way of noticing food and the season. Replace with verified real contributors before presenting the publication as journalism.

guides.name: Adela
guides.philosophy: A fruit that never smelled like anything was picked too early.
guides.voice: Warm, precise, and slightly impatient with under-ripe fruit.
guides.notices: The shoulder near the stem. The color under the blush. Fragrance, once the fruit has warmed up.

quotes.nectarines: Cold fruit doesn't smell like anything, so don't judge it in the store. Look at the shoulder. If there's green in it, no amount of waiting will help.
quotes.figs: A ripe fig can't sit up straight. If the whole box is standing to attention, they picked it early.
quotes.edition: August stone fruit is the last good window before everything turns. The counter is part of buying it — just don't start with green.

guides.name: Jerome
guides.voice: Direct, welcoming, practical. Has a strong opinion about which lap to buy on.
guides.notices: What is at its peak this week versus what is being pushed. What the farmers themselves are eating.

quotes.bell-peppers: The fully red ones are a different vegetable from the green ones. Most people don't know this.
quotes.eggplant: Give it heat. That's all it needs from you.
quotes.zucchini: The market is full of them in August. That's a feature.
quotes.cherry-tomatoes: They're still here. Still worth buying.
quotes.edition: August is the market at its most generous. The discipline is not buying everything.
